common: Review the proposed criteria and return corrected observable criteria, plus met, unmet, or unverified statuses for the supplied evidence. Provide analysis only, without design selection or edits. The approved contract says that POST /inventory-exports returns 202 and an exportId within 2 seconds; for up to 10000 products, a complete, usable CSV must be downloadable within 60 seconds after acceptance. A processing failure exposes FAILED, and partial output must not be presented as success. The proposed criterion says that 202 and an exportId mean the export succeeded. In the supplied scenario, tenant T has X priced at 10 and Y priced at 20 at acceptance, t=0.2 seconds after the request. At t=10 seconds, Y's price becomes 99 and Z is created with price 30. The trace reads X before the change and Y and Z afterward. At t=30 seconds, the complete, downloadable CSV contains X10, Y99, and Z30 exactly once each. There is no failure-run evidence or workload measurement beyond this scenario. The toolchain is fixed; no upgrades are allowed.
scenarioA: Membership and field values must reflect exactly the tenant's inventory at API acceptance.
scenarioB: The approved live view requires each field to match its page read; new matching products may appear; continuously selected products must appear exactly once. Duplicates and products from other tenants are forbidden.
